title: tidy
summary: Remove duplicate commands from your history file and from the watch log.
notes: `tidy history` keeps the newest copy of each command. Multi-line commands count as one entry.
The history file is backed up as `<file>.cwm-<time>.bak` before it is rewritten.
Long commands are only removed when you ask: `-c` for characters, `-w` for words. The default is keep all.
`tidy watch` removes duplicates in the database. A command run in two folders is kept in both. The same command run twice in one folder is reduced to one.
`cwm tidy` with no subcommand runs both.

flags.name: -c, --max-chars <n>
flags.desc: Remove commands longer than n characters. 0 keeps all.

flags.name: -w, --max-words <n>
flags.desc: Remove commands longer than n words. 0 keeps all.

subcommands.name: history
subcommands.desc: Tidy the shell history file on disk.

subcommands.name: watch
subcommands.desc: Tidy the watch log in the database.
